title: How eslint treats Herdr's empty catch blocks in the cloned spaces mod
body:
**Chose:** a files-scoped override for `mods/factory-spaces/main.js` only, setting `no-empty` to `allowEmptyCatch: true`, so every other rule and empty non-catch blocks still fail.
**Over:** editing Herdr's code (breaks the clean re-clone diff), or turning `no-empty` off for the file.
**Because:** the slice names this override; `@eslint/js` recommended flags the two empty `catch {}` at lines 126 and 149, and this is the narrowest setting that passes them.
**Undo:** delete the override block in `eslint.config.js`.

title: Where install.sh records what it wrote
body:
**Chose:** `factory-install.txt` in the Herdr home, one installed path per line (`mods/factory-spaces`, `layouts/factory.json`), rewritten after each install. A target that exists and is not listed is foreign; every target is checked before anything is written.
**Over:** a JSON manifest, or marking ownership with a file inside each mod folder (cannot mark a single layout file or a symlink).
**Because:** bash reads it with `grep -x` and no python; the slice asked only for "a manifest file in that home".
**Undo:** change the `manifest` path and `owned()` in `install.sh`.

title: shellcheck reads `herdr-app do ...` as a stray `do` keyword (SC1010)
Which strip a run shows when several states apply, and where a stopped run goes
body:
**Chose:** a live run follows factory's own status line order (`glance`, factory `src/cli/status.rs:373`): an open question, then parked, then paused, then driver dead, else building (starting, checkpoint and closeout too, with their phase shown). A run that is over is failed when its phase is `failed` or it was stopped (`stopped` sets phase `finished`), shipped otherwise. A space lists its strips most urgent first (owner, dead, failed, parked, paused, building, shipped), and the rail dot takes the first one's color: `blocked` for the first three, `muted` for parked and paused, `working`, `done`.
**Over:** the table's row order as precedence (building first would swallow every other live state), or a separate state for stopped runs (the table has none).
**Because:** the strip then agrees with the line `factory status` prints for the same run; a stopped run with no PR has nothing to show as shipped.
**Undo:** `classify()` and `RANK`/`TONE` in `mods/factory-spaces/lib/runs.js`.

title: How a too-old factory is recognised when it refuses --recent
body:
**Chose:** when `factory status --json --recent` exits non-zero, ask `factory status --json` once and read the envelope's `factory` version from that; below 0.13.0 is too old. A second failure, or no factory at all, draws nothing.
**Over:** reading the version only from the `--recent` call's envelope.
**Because:** factory 0.12.0 has no `--recent` flag (`git show v0.12.0:src/cli/status.rs`), so clap refuses the call and no envelope comes back to compare.
**Undo:** `readStatus()` in `mods/factory-spaces/lib/runs.js`.

title: A runs layout prop for the folder factory-spaces watches
body:
**Chose:** `factory-spaces` watches `props().runs` when the layout sets it, else `home() + "/.local/share/factory/runs"`, beside the `factory` prop the PRD names.
**Over:** only the home path.
**Because:** the harness points factory at fixture runs with `FACTORY_DATA_DIR`; a mod has no environment, so without the prop an event appended to a fixture run reaches the strip only at the next 10 s poll, and FR-3's 2 s acceptance cannot be proved on the harness.
**Undo:** drop `props()?.runs ??` in `watchRuns()` in `mods/factory-spaces/main.js`.

title: Scratch window on its own hc core, not only its own home
body:
**Chose:** each scratch window gets its own hc core too: `HC_SESSION=vhf-<run>` and a scratch `XDG_STATE_HOME`, besides the scratch `HERDR_APP_HOME`. Cleanup stops that core and every process whose environment carries the session.
**Over:** a scratch `HERDR_APP_HOME` alone, as §12 words it.
**Because:** herdr-app keeps spaces in the core's document, not in the home (AGENTS.md, The model). On the owner's core, a scratch window would show the owner's spaces, and a `space.new` from the harness would land in the owner's window. herdr-app reaches the core through `hc connect`, so the variable gets through; doctor checks that the core answering is a process of that session.
**Undo:** drop `HC_SESSION` and `XDG_STATE_HOME` from `SCRATCH_ENV` in `.claude/skills/verify-herdr-factory/bin/lib.sh`, and the core steps from `cleanup.sh`.

title: Fixture runs: 8 runs on 3 repos, registered in factory.db
body:
**Chose:** 8 fixture runs over 3 git repos: shop (building, owner needed, shipped), api (paused, parked, driver dead, failed), loner (one building run, never opened as a space). Each run also gets a `runs` row and one `workers` row in the fixture `factory.db`, written with `sqlite3`, and the open BLOCK gets its `log.jsonl` entry and slice files through `factory docs log add`.
**Over:** one of the seven state runs in the repo with no space, and fixture runs with no `factory.db` rows.
**Because:** a state whose run sits in the repo with no space could never be screenshotted for the run-strip proof, so the run with no space is an eighth. Without the db rows `factory answer` fails with `sqlite: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed` after it has already appended `block_answered`, and every budget reads 0 used.
**Undo:** move runs between repos in `build()` in `tests/fixtures/factory-fixtures.sh` and update `expected` in `tests/fixtures/check-fixtures.js`. Dropping `register.sql` breaks the answer flow.

title: A backgrounded shell function's pid is the shell, not the program
body: Backgrounding a shell function (`in_scratch herdr-app &`) records the forked shell as `$!`, not the window; background the env array directly (`"${SCRATCH_ENV[@]}" setsid herdr-app &`), as `launch.sh` does.

title: overlay.close does not close the first-run welcome
body: A fresh herdr-app home opens on the welcome dialog, and `overlay.close` answers ok but leaves it up; seed `shared.json` with `frame.welcomed` and `update-notes.json` with `last_run` before launch (`launch.sh` does).

title: after slice-03
body:
**Covers:** slices 01, 02, 03
**Gate:** 1 run, 0 red, minutes not in the transcript (the test tier took 0.8 s; 37 tests, runs.js at 100% lines, 94.81% branches) — caught: nothing
**Prove:** FR-1, FR-2, FR-3, FR-4 — evidence: cp-1/install-transcript.txt, cp-1/install-stale-hash.txt, cp-1/layout-main-no-runs.png, cp-1/layout-factory-no-runs.png, cp-1/layout-compare.txt, cp-1/runs-on-spaces-before.png, cp-1/runs-on-spaces-after.png, cp-1/runs-append-a001.txt, cp-1/runs-append-before.png, cp-1/runs-append-after.png, cp-1/runs-append-timing.txt, cp-1/strip-{building,owner-needed,paused,parked,driver-dead,shipped,failed}-{light,dark}.png (14), cp-1/strips-all-light.png, cp-1/strips-all-dark.png, cp-1/strips.txt, cp-1/strips-factory-status.json, cp-1/rail-dots-dark.png
**Fixed:** leaks: tests/fixtures/check-fixtures.js:31 (checks the number of open questions, not a literal id) · leaks: tests/fixtures/factory-fixtures.sh:174 (the event's block id is the one `factory docs log add` prints) · leaks: tests/fixtures/status-0.12.0.json:18, tests/fixtures/status-0.13.0.json:63, :66, :70 and tests/runs.test.js:177 (static fixture question id `Q-1`). No Prove row failed.

Notes for the reviewer: FR-2 and FR-4 used a copy of the checkout whose `layouts/factory.json` spaces block also sets `props.factory` and `props.runs` to a fixture wrapper, so the scratch window never read the owner's real runs; FR-2's copy also had a stale `spaces` hash in `upstream.json`. The agents block was hidden with `layout.hide` so both spaces' strips fit the frame. `herdr-app status` in install.sh starts an hc core for whatever `HC_SESSION` is set when no window answers; FR-1's scratch core was stopped afterwards.

title: Which question Answer answers when a run has several open
body:
**Chose:** the strip's Answer opens the dialog for the run's first open question, the one whose text the strip shows; the others are answered one after another, each as the next first once the previous is resolved.
**Over:** a picker of the open questions in the dialog, or one Answer button per question.
**Because:** the strip already names every open id but shows only the first question's text, and the slice gives the dialog one question; the order is factory's `questions` order.
**Undo:** `answer()` in `mods/factory-spaces/main.js` takes `r.questions[0]`.

title: What a question alerts with when its run has no space, and when alerts wait
body:
**Chose:** a question on a run that shows under no space still toasts and plays `blocked`, with no `action`; and the mod decides alerts only once every local space with a folder has had its git read, retrying after each git look until then.
**Over:** holding the alert until a space for the run appears (it may never: a repo with no space), or alerting at the first poll even before the spaces' git is read.
**Because:** the owner still needs to hear of a question in a repo with no space; and at start-up the first poll can return before any space's git top is known, so the run's space would read as missing and the toast would be marked seen with nothing to click through to.
**Undo:** the `space ? { action } : {}` in `alerts()` in `mods/factory-spaces/lib/alerts.js`, and `raiseDue` in `raise()` and `refreshGit()` in `mods/factory-spaces/main.js`.

title: Whether a dismissed run that is live again shows
body:
**Chose:** a dismissed id hides a run only while it classifies as shipped or failed; were it live again its strip shows, and the id stays until the run drops out of the list.
**Over:** hiding a dismissed run whatever its state.
**Because:** × is drawn only on finished strips, so the owner never dismissed a live one; a hidden live run could hide an open question.
**Undo:** the `finished(r)` check in `undismissed()` in `mods/factory-spaces/lib/alerts.js`.

title: How the harness clicks and types in the scratch window
body:
**Chose:** an opt-in launch mode, `VERIFY_HERDR_INPUT=x11 bin/launch.sh`, that starts a private rootful `Xwayland :N` and opens the scratch window on it with `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` unset. `bin/input.sh` clicks and types there through a small XTest tool, `bin/xdrive.c`, built into the scratch on first use. `bin/restart.sh` quits and restarts the window on the same home, core and display. The default launch is unchanged.
**Over:** proving the toast's click by running its `space.select` with `do` (a different path from the one the row names), injecting input through the owner's Hyprland (off limits: it moves the owner's pointer), or reporting the click-only rows unreached.
**Because:** the toast click, × and Answer (and the dialog's typing) are reachable only by pointer and keys. `herdr-app commands` has no click or key command. A private X server keeps every injected event off the owner's display.
**Undo:** delete `input.sh`, `restart.sh` and `xdrive.c`, the `VERIFY_HERDR_INPUT` block in `launch.sh`, and `x_display`, `start_window` and `stop_window` in `lib.sh`, and use the old inline start in `launch.sh` again.

**Review:** fyi

title: after slice-05
body:
**Covers:** slices 04, 05
**Gate:** 1 run, 0 red, minutes not in the transcript (the test tier took 0.9 s; 60 tests, alerts.js and answer.js at 100% lines, all files 97.99% branches) — caught: nothing
**Prove:** FR-5, FR-6, FR-7 — evidence: cp-2/alert-before.png, cp-2/alert-open-block.txt, cp-2/alert-toast.png, cp-2/alert-clicked-space.png, cp-2/alert-restart.txt, cp-2/alert-after-restart-1s.png, cp-2/alert-after-restart-3s.png, cp-2/alert-factory-status.json, cp-2/alert-unit-test.txt, cp-2/dismiss-seed.txt, cp-2/dismiss-before.png, cp-2/dismiss-drive.txt, cp-2/dismiss-after.png, cp-2/dismiss-after-restart.png, cp-2/answer-dialog-open.png, cp-2/answer-dialog-typed.png, cp-2/answer-sent-toast.png, cp-2/answer-sent-strip.png, cp-2/answer-drive.txt, cp-2/answers-BLOCK-1.json, cp-2/answer-resolved-dialog-open.png, cp-2/answer-resolved-refused.png, cp-2/answer-resolved-drive.txt, cp-2/answers-BLOCK-1-resolved-run.json (each PNG with the `.txt` of status and ls beside it)
**Fixed:** leaks: tests/alerts.test.js:30, :40, :44, :52, :59, :60, :74, :76, :85, :93, :97, :101 · leaks: tests/answer.test.js:11, :13, :16, :18, :24, :28, :35, :52, :53, :69 (static question ids `Q-1`, `Q-2`, `Q-3`; 22 hits). No Prove row failed. The harness could not click or type, and the toast, ×, Answer and the dialog take only pointer and keys. It now opens the window on a private Xwayland display for that (`VERIFY_HERDR_INPUT=x11`, `bin/input.sh`, `bin/restart.sh`, `bin/xdrive.c`, recipe `features/run-actions.md`), AD-11.

Notes for the reviewer: FR-5 and FR-7 ran on scratch run cp2, FR-6's resolved case on a fresh cp2b. Both used a copy of the checkout whose `layouts/factory.json` sets `props.factory` and `props.runs` to the fixture wrapper and runs folder, installed with `install.sh` into the scratch home. FR-7 needed a second shipped run on shop, which the fixtures lack, so `006-20261106-a004` (a copy of `005-…-a003` with PR 101 and its `factory.db` rows) was seeded before the drive (cp-2/dismiss-seed.txt). For FR-6's resolved case, the block was answered from a shell while the dialog was open, the way an owner answering in a terminal races the window. The private X server opens as one more window on the owner's desktop, and cleanup stopped it (only the owner's `Xwayland :0` remained).
